title: Typography and Text Styling
subtitle: Control fonts, sizes, spacing, alignment and text appearance.
description: Learn how to create readable and professional typography using font families, weights, line heights and text properties.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Typography and Text Styling

Welcome to Lesson 5: Typography and Text Styling. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Typography and Text Styling”. The goal is to control fonts, sizes, spacing, alignment and text appearance.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Typography affects readability through font choice, size, weight, line height, spacing, and line length. A clear hierarchy helps people distinguish a page title, section headings, body text, and secondary information.

blocks.question: Paragraphs are hard to scan because lines stretch across a very wide desktop screen. What would help?
options: Constrain line length and provide comfortable line-height.
Make the text smaller until it fits.
Remove paragraph breaks.
Set every word in uppercase.
blocks.explanation: A readable line length and adequate line-height improve sustained reading.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A readable line length and adequate line-height improve sustained reading.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A readable line length and adequate line-height improve sustained reading.

blocks.question: A page heading and body copy look equally important. What should be tuned?
options: Only the footer border.
A consistent type hierarchy using size, weight, spacing, and semantic headings.
Randomly change every font.
Add extra punctuation.
blocks.explanation: A deliberate typographic hierarchy helps users understand information structure.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A deliberate typographic hierarchy helps users understand information structure.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A deliberate typographic hierarchy helps users understand information structure.

blocks.text: Use a sensible fallback font stack and avoid making body text too small. Line height should give paragraphs enough breathing room, while excessively wide lines make it harder to find the next line.

blocks.question: Text clips after the user zooms the page. What should the developer test?
options: Only the default desktop width.
Whether all text has a fixed height.
Responsive sizing, zoom, and content wrapping.
Whether the title contains a period.
blocks.explanation: Accessible text must remain readable when users zoom or font sizes change.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Accessible text must remain readable when users zoom or font sizes change.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning

blocks.question: A learner’s XP changes after every correct answer. Which design is easiest to maintain?
options: Repeat the current XP number in many places.
Store XP in one appropriately scoped variable and update it deliberately.
Use a different variable name for every update.
Convert XP to a text label before doing arithmetic.
blocks.explanation: One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. One well-defined source of truth prevents values from drifting apart.

blocks.question: A setting must never be reassigned during the program. What should you choose?
options: A constant or immutable binding supported by the language.
A global variable that any function can change.
A string containing the setting name.
A loop that resets the value repeatedly.
blocks.explanation: Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Constants communicate intent and help prevent accidental reassignment.
